result.question: Map the current (September 2026) pi agent family by Mario Zechner (badlogic) — pi-mono repo, CLI/TUI, Agent UI, pi-ai SDK, related npm packages — plus its community ecosystem; run a hard-requirements gap analysis (hooks/extension interception, context compaction, session management), assess macOS + native Windows viability and provider support (openai-codex, local models, multi-provider), compare against Claude Code where gaps exist, and end with adopt/extend/dealbreaker recommendations grounded in primary sources.
result.summary: Split the question along its deliverables: primary-source mapping of the repo/packages, the author's own writing for intent and cadence, a deep-dive on the extension/hooks mechanism (the make-or-break MUST-HAVE), platform + provider viability, and community ecosystem plus skeptical comparison against Claude Code. Each angle targets a different source class (repo/docs, blog/mastodon, API source, issue trackers, third-party artifacts) so results complement rather than overlap.

results.title: pi-mono: packages/coding-agent/docs/extensions.md (extension API, primary source)
results.snippet: The canonical extension API doc. Extensions are TypeScript modules receiving an ExtensionAPI; pi.on() intercepts events to block or modify tool calls (denylist/allowlist, path guards, destructive-command confirmation = pre-tool-call permission gating), plus session lifecycle handlers (session_start/session_shutdown), custom tools, slash commands, UI interaction via ctx.ui, and custom providers. Directly answers whether pi's extensions cover the four Claude Code hook classes.

results.title: pi-mono: docs/compaction.md — context compaction design
results.snippet: Primary source for MUST-HAVE (b): pi summarizes older content when the context window fills, appending a CompactionEntry (summary + firstKeptEntryId) and reloading the session from the summary. Extensions can intercept compaction — cancel it or supply a custom summary — which also confirms a compaction lifecycle event exists for hooks.

results.title: pi-mono: docs/sessions.md — session persist/list/resume
results.snippet: Primary source for MUST-HAVE (c): `pi -c` continues the most recent session, `pi -r` / `/resume` open an interactive session picker, `pi --session <path|id>` opens a specific one; sessions are persisted trees (id/parentId) with `/tree` navigation, and SessionManager exposes continueRecent/inMemory plus cross-project listing via the SDK.

results.snippet: Long-form practitioner comparison after 100 hours of real use: Pi scored 6 vs Claude Code's 5 on their tool-use benchmark at ~1/5 the cost, but concludes Claude Code remains the better daily driver for most people (guardrails, subscription pricing, polish) — a useful counterweight that names the adoption trade-offs and dealbreakers.

results.snippet: Concrete proof that pi-tui carries real win32 console-mode support (GetStdHandle/GetConsoleMode/SetConsoleMode via koffi for VT key input like Shift+Tab) and that Windows is actively maintained rather than best-effort — the issue (May 2026) is about slimming the native helper, not adding Windows support.

results.snippet: Surfaces a real limitation on the Codex-subscription auth path: browser-based OAuth means pi cannot currently authenticate with a ChatGPT subscription on remote/headless hosts; device-code login is a requested but unshipped fix — relevant to auth-path viability and any server/CI usage.

results.title: pi-ollama-provider issue #6: native vs extension-based Ollama integration
results.snippet: Community-ecosystem evidence on the local-model axis: 30+ user-filed Ollama-related issues against pi and a third-party provider extension debating official-extension vs core integration — shows both demand and the extension mechanism being used for provider work, and is a candidate community asset to adopt or learn from.

results.title: What I learned building an opinionated and minimal coding agent (Mario Zechner, 2025-11-30)
results.snippet: The founding primary source: Zechner's own design-philosophy post for pi. Explains the radical-minimalism stance — sub-1000-token system prompt, four built-in tools, everything else via the TypeScript extension system — and the explicit 'NO list' (no MCP, no sub-agents, no plan mode, no permission popups, no background bash). Directly answers why hooks/gating must come from extensions, and documents that compaction, tree-structured sessions, skills, and multi-provider auth ARE built in. Also reveals origin intent: built because Claude Code's feature velocity made it unpredictable — a stability-over-features maintenance signal.

results.title: I've sold out (Mario Zechner, 2026-04-08) — pi joins Earendil Inc.
results.snippet: The single most important long-term-viability signal from the author: as of April 2026 pi moved to Earendil Inc., a venture-backed public benefit corporation co-founded by Armin Ronacher (Flask). Zechner works on pi full-time, retains technical direction, MIT license retained. Changes the maintenance-health assessment from 'solo indie side project' to 'company-backed with full-time maintainer' — central to the adopt-now recommendation.

result.caveats: Time-sensitivity: all metrics (stars, versions, push dates) are a 2026-09-01 snapshot of a project releasing at very high cadence; re-check before acting on version-specific details. Premise staleness: the research question's repo/npm coordinates (badlogic/pi-mono, @mariozechner) are superseded — every finding here was re-anchored to earendil-works/pi and @earendil-works. Hooks coverage is the biggest verification gap: only pre-tool-call blocking (tool_call) and session_before_compact were mechanically verified among the four required hook classes; post-edit format/lint/test triggers, session start/stop lifecycle events, and outward notification/observability hooks are plausible from the extensions event system but were NOT confirmed by any surviving claim — do not treat them as established. The community-ecosystem deliverable is thin: the packaging substrate and Discord are verified, but no census of third-party extensions/themes/forks survived verification, so 'which community assets to adopt' is answered only anecdotally. The 'Pi Agent UI' deliverable is partially unanswered: pi-web-ui exists but is a component library lagging ~3 months behind core; no standalone first-party UI app was verified on any platform. Some supporting evidence (docs/extensions.md blocking contract, docs/providers.md Ollama example, issue numbers) came from verifiers' corroboration fetches rather than the original voted claims — same primary-source class, but single-pass reads. One claim was refuted 0-3 (a wrong @earendil/pi package name), illustrating scope-name confusion risk in secondary coverage. Governance change risk: Earendil Works stewardship (post 'I've sold out') was verified as fact, but its licensing/roadmap implications were not examined.
